reviews.text: bussin frfr

[h1]四个骰子，百种变化[/h1] Luck & Loot以骰子构筑为核心，为我们呈现了一款小而美的回合制肉鸽游戏。 玩家可以选择一个初始职业，携带四个初始骰子，每个骰子有6个面可以DIY骰面。 通过把技能拖拽到骰面上，来构成自己的打法，每个技能需要占用不同的容量，而每个骰子初始有21点容量，后续可以通过遗物、升级骰子来扩容。 在战斗中，每回合四个骰子投掷的结果，将决定玩家可以做出哪些行动。 丰富多样的技能和自由搭配的玩法，为游戏带来了百种变化。 [h1]有容错率的战斗[/h1] 骰子掷下后，玩家可以有2次机会进行重随，而重随可以整体重随，也可以只随空格子（有些情况下，因为技能容量不同，骰子装不满6个技能）。 敲定当前回合的行动后，在回合结束前，还允许玩家进行一次悔棋（一局只能一次）。 敌人的意图会显示在其脚下，助于玩家做出行动决策。 每个职业有不同的职业技能，职业技能会随着走房间次数而恢复CD。 但是注意，游戏中有疲劳机制，如果鏖战超过7回合，那么双方则会在回合开始时都获得一个随机debuff。 虽然有叠盾技能，但护盾有上限，不能无限叠，护盾上限往往通过遗物或者事件来提升。 [h1]简易的路径选择[/h1] 在关卡内，一般是一本道一路走到黑，越往后的关卡，层数越多，并且中间会有一次路径选择的机会（类爬塔地图），但也只有二选一，降低玩家决策的疲劳。 每关打完可以在大地图上选关，但是关卡难度不同，所以基本上没办法跳关，除非你能很快就build出超模的搭配。 [h1]局外解锁[/h1] 解锁更多技能：冒险结束后，会结算局外经验，局外经验升级则解锁更多的局内技能。 解锁更多英雄：使用一个职业打通关，就会解锁下一个角色。 [h1]一只复古但有趣的麻雀[/h1] 本作的美术采用了极简像素风，还做了一个CRT凸面屏的视觉效果，旨在契合游戏的复古设计。 在局内会遇到一些有趣的事件，比如其中有一个撬锁玩法，玩家有3次机会试错，需要试出长度为3的密码组合，例如：←→←，由于给了3次机会破解，所以只要有耐心，基本能解开。 作为一款回合制肉鸽游戏，本作的玩法设计也是五脏俱全，金币、回血、盾、事件、遗物、诅咒、敌人意图，基本上大家耳熟能详的机制，它都有。 本作的难度数值曲线较为陡峭，打到第三关时就会变得异常吃力。 好在其最核心的骰子构筑玩法较有深度，提供了一定的可玩性，给骰子喂技能后，还可以为这个骰子提供永久加成，例如给骰子上的每个技能追加一个debuff技能，或使得骰子上的每个技能都能为玩家+1护盾。 总的来说值得一试，不过目前不支持简中，但英语生词不多，能接受的可以啃着玩。 [quote] 奏游戏之乐章，品人生之绚烂 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45672460/]欢迎加入 『 丰川集团 』[/url] [u][b]以丰川集团之名，行评测鉴赏之事[/b][/u][/quote]

[h1] [b]骰筑策略与混沌的华丽碰撞，赌狗与欧皇的终极修罗场[/b][/h1] 作为一款“骰子构筑”Roguelike，《Luck & Loot》游戏节奏偏快，游戏中需要玩家扮演三位受诅咒的英雄之一，深入变幻莫测的地牢深处。游戏的核心玩法在于骰子的构筑，收集、升级、替换80+种骰面，精心打造四枚专属骰子，所以游戏中的狗运也很重要，不然玩家精心设计的骰面，捣鼓半天，摇出来个1点，直接给Boss都整笑了：“刮痧呢老弟？”玩过《骰子地下城》可能对本作更容易上手，本作的游戏深度比《骰子地下城》要深一些，但是基础玩法类似。本作的策略深度藏在“动态构筑”的钢丝绳上，除了骰子强化之外，还有灾厄修正和随机事件需要玩家应对，游戏嘴上说“策略与混沌碰撞”，实则“运气才是真主角”。 游戏的美工画风偏向克苏鲁，黑暗奇幻风格的像素游戏，很有复古的气息，伴随着诡异的BGM，游戏的氛围感拉满，打完一局耳朵和理智一起蒸发。 总的来说，本作是一款快节奏的骰子Roguelike冒险游戏，玩法简单却富有深度，骰面构筑能玩出花来，但是同样的，本作的运气成分比较多，化身赌狗与系统一战吧。 [quote]欢迎关注『 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45525570/] 桃你欢心 [/url]』 [b] 桃影扶风评百戏，落墨如歌写人间[/b][/quote]

The game is really fun an very unique. I love to be able to roll dice an customize it after each battle. if you are tired of online PvP games and need a relax game to play and chill, I highly recommend this game!

[h1][b]《Luck & Loot》——骰子已经掷出，命运由你掌控！[/b][/h1] [h3]【游戏玩法】[/h3] [list] [*][b]地图：[/b]这片冒险大陆上一共有5个场景关卡，分别是森林（Forest）、墓园（Graveyard）、沼泽（Swamp）、废墟（Ruins）、暗黑之塔（Dark Keep），难度等级依次递增，且只有通过前一场景后才能进入下一幕。每个场景都有独特的怪物和特殊事件，比如森林的树桩怪、蘑菇怪，墓园的掘墓夺宝，沼泽的淤泥怪、毒黄蜂等等，画面虽然是8比特的复古像素风，也能看出作者的用心设计。 [*][b]骰面编辑：[/b]以战士为例，有4个6面骰子，前期很容易摇出画着“X”的没有任何效果的空骰面，点开右下角的“DICE”可以发现，这些骰子并不是所有面上都安装了效果，要想不掷出空骰，就需要用把每个面上都装上效果。每个效果都有对应的能力值（Capacity），往往效果越强，占用的能力值越高；而每个骰子都有能力值（Dice Capacity）的限制，初始上限是20，那么一个骰子上的能力点数之和就不能超过20（后期有饰品等道具可以提升能力值上限）；如何充分利用4个骰子的能力值以装上总和数更多的效果，还有强力效果的取舍，都是需要考虑的问题。另外，如果需要每回合都有稳定的回血或输出，也可以考虑将相同效果聚集在同一个骰子上。所以综合而言，发挥空间还是很大的。 [*][b]战斗：[/b]玩家与怪物的对战，双方均是通过摇骰子出招的。不仅玩家会摇出空骰，怪物也会，故可以将本回合不攻击的怪靠后攻击。如果摇出空骰，可直接选择重摇空骰（Roll Empty）；点击浮起的骰子使之落下，此时按重掷（Roll）时不会重置该骰子，可借此刷效果。人物的护甲是有上限的，且新回合不归零。 [*][b]事件：[/b]有的是石堆封路，可以选择自己挖（扣血）或是请人挖（扣钱）；有的是扣血挖坟概率获得金币或道具；还有许愿池投币、与哥布林赌博等等。其中最有意思的是撬宝箱，有向左、向右两个选择，连续猜对3次方向就能打开，失误一次就得重新来（方向和顺序不变，可试出答案），共有3次机会；如果机会用尽，也可选择扣血强拆宝箱。 [/list] [h3]【不足之处】[/h3] [olist] [*]没有汉化，对于中文玩家要理解文本和剧情还是有一定难度的（现已更新，支持中文）。 [*]无法提前看到升级后的属性加成，不便于挑选要升级的骰面，建议加上。 [*]界面布局不太合理。游戏的主要画面只占整个屏幕的1/3，留白过多。 [*]进入、退出游戏或更改设置经常会导致死机，只能强制退出。 [/olist] [quote] 恭请雅鉴 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45531068/]黑白测评[/url] [hr]黑夜显真 白昼辨伪

A high-quality riff on the "dicebuilder" sub-genre, largely comparable to Slash & Dice in core mechanics, boasting a good, cohesive aesthetic and a good challenge. My biggest initial issues with the game are that: (1) the actual amount of content feels very low, even for a game that's only $8, in comparison to its genre peers, and (2) the game commits the [b]cardinal sin[/b] of dice and deckbuilder games (and, arguably, roguelites in general) and encouraging endless, un-fun grinding mid-run. To elaborate on my second point; there are various heal and armor skills (including those you start with) which may be used over and over in a given battle. Thus, if you leave only one enemy alive with low damage potential (which you can also enforce with debuffs like Weak) you can just choose not to make attacks and take turn after turn after turn rerolling and using your heal and armor skills to fully heal after every fight (which the game evidently does not expect/assume you to do, based on how many events and merchant effects allow you to spend resources to heal). This becomes worse in light of an early-game, common skill available to the first character, which lets you permanently increase your maximum armor (which carries between combats) if you use it at full armor. Again, with the aforementioned "leave a weak enemy alive" strategy, this can be grinded for as long as you have pateince, as long as you have adequate defensive skills. There's a very rare skill that can also increase your max HP in a similar way. The developers appear to have tried to mitigate this by having a penalty for staying in battles too long - a system employed by various games (including Darkest Dungeon and Across the Obelisk) to prevent players from optimising the fun out of their own game. But the penalty takes a long while to ramp up - for multiple turns you get a tiny debuff or a point of damage every turn, both of which can be adequately mitigated by sufficiently defensive builds. The result is a game with a challenge seemingly based around damage-rushing and damage-optimizing against enemies, but the optimum strategy appears to be a glacially slow clicker to slowly heal and permanently-buff your character at the end of every combat for turn after turn after turn after turn.

[h1][b]自定义骰子的迷你地下城[/b][/h1] 《Luck & Loot》是一款迷你的Rogue冒险游戏，玩家可以打造属于自己的骰子，然后在随机生成的地下城中展开冒险，享受构筑与策略带来的乐趣。 本作采用了大颗粒像素风作为画面主基调，非常有经典老游戏的味道，不过这并不代表简陋，游戏为角色、敌人、环境等内容均添加了动画效果，加上多个可选的风格滤镜，观感还是挺不错的。 游戏打造了多个区域，诸如森林、墓地、沼泽、遗迹、城堡等，进入区域后可以看到角色在动画区域不断前进，遇到敌人、宝藏、商人、遭遇等事件后便会停下来等待玩家操作。 战斗为回合制，敌我双方都会掷骰子展开行动，敌人的骰子结果会显示在画面中供玩家参考。 角色拥有4个骰子，系统会默认掷出一次，玩家可选择全部重掷或是只重掷空白骰面的骰子，觉得结果满意后便可以拖动骰子到目标身上来作战了。 骰面的效果多种多样，诸如直接造成伤害、施加流血效果、治疗、护盾等。 一开始骰子的骰面并不是完全满的，因此便会出现掷出空白的情况，战斗获胜、宝箱、商店等事件中都可以获得新的骰面，玩家可将其随意放置到骰子上。 此外遇敌后系统还允许玩家根据敌方阵容来调整骰子，这点相当人性化了。 游戏目前设计了3个不同的角色，那便是经典的战士、法师、射手三人组了，每个角色都有不同的战斗风格。 整体来说《Luck & Loot》给人的感觉精致小巧，自定义骰子、根据敌方意图予以反制的玩法也挺不错，推荐喜欢Rogue构筑和复古风画面的玩家入手。 [quote]热爱游戏，畅玩游戏，分享游戏，专注鉴赏评测与深度解析 欢迎关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44110339/]游理游据[/url]，走进游戏世界，品味第九艺术[/quote]

I was really disappointed with Luck & Loot. There is nothing new here. It's competently executed, it's got a specific aesthetic that it uses ok. But I've played 20 games in the past year that do everything this game does, but adds something to the formula. L&L is bog standard. It's a basic deckbuilder roguelite dungeon crawl. And it's too easy. There's nothing wrong with it -- it just doesn't stand out.
aggressively addictive and then the nerfs ruined it. (im basing this off being able to easily beat the game with 6/6 modifiers and now i cant even get past the second stage with all mods off)

Play here: https://youtu.be/dd1bId_Qvx0 Honestly there's so much good in this game and it's utterly ruined by balancing I'd definitely check it out again and update my review, but the creator needs to figure out his fatigue system I understand the purpose of it it's so the player doesn't sit stack max armor or fully heal off every battle, but IT"S WAY too early in the fights each fight can have multiple enemies they all have a solid amount of hp and can play defensively/heal. I should be getting blasted my damage/debuffs at turn 8. There's no way to mitigate debuff damage besides healing, but healing is a weak effect and putting healing on your dice mitigates your damage and because of fatigure you're pretty much pigeon holed into an offensive build. I'm not saying it's impossible or not doable, but to me it's incredibly unfun and relies a lot on rng that can't be mitigated by player skill at the moment. It's a dice game it's supposed to have rng, but the point of RNG in these types of games (to my preference anyways) is for the player to figure out and mitigate the RNG to the best of his abilities which is really hindered in the current state of the game. The dialogue is awesome I enjoy how many events there are and how rewards are handed out/the upgrade system the art style is really cool too balancing at the moment in my opinion is just atrocious.
相当不错的肉鸽回合制地牢探险游戏，投骰子的方式虽然有点随机性，但是可以通过升级把随机性降到比较低。三个角色也各有特点，把他们都升到最高级后，感觉战士相对弱一点，游侠靠闪避基本打人都不会掉血，法师的易伤流能在两回合就速杀最终boss。普通难度通关n次之后又虐了几次最终boss，满足卸载。

I'm afraid I disagree with a lot of design choice here and therefore I cannot recommend this. 1. For a game with Loot in the title, there just isn't enough loot around. Why do I have to pick between gold and a skill after every battle? Surely it would make more sense to give a base gold reward and give me the option to decide between a skill and extra gold? I'm always running low on gold and end up bankrupt at the merchant, while simultaneously not having enough skills around to upgrade the dice (see below). 2. Destroying dice skills to upgrade dice is a nice concept, but I just don't have enough spare skills lying around to upgrade my dice. 3. Skill upgrades are not balanced. Some skills get a measly +1 damage upgrade while others receive a damage upgrade, effect upgrade AND capacity reduction. It's always incredibly obvious which skill to upgrade when given the chance and there aren't that many opportunities to upgrade either. 3. The events are questionable. I am constantly losing gold and health. Usually when you gamble in games, you receive a bonus while having the risk of losing something. Why is it that I am constantly losing health in this game without receiving any benefits? There's also not much variety in the events, so the optimum play is just to avoid the random events. I'm also not convinced by the RNG because how did I manage to "win" the 5% lottery* and lose health multiple times in a row from the magic machine?! Perhaps I just lack the Luck required for this game? 4. There isn't that much content in the first place and yet all of it is locked behind play time. Due to the combined issues above, I only won 1 of the ~10 games I played and that was an extremely lucky lvl 1 archer run. To summarise, I find this game very unbalanced and lacking content. I will instead direct you to an underrated game called Dicefolk, which has so much more content and strategic depth. *The actual % might be 3% or 10%. I am done with the game for good, so I did not check again.
这个价位还是很不错的小游戏，就是职业需要升级解锁比较脑壳疼

This game feels nearly perfect in all respects. But meta-progression kinda bugs me. Not that I don't think it should be present, but the power scaling of it should be flattened. It sucks to play your best and think you actually have a chance, only to find that the next tier of unlocks make it very clear that the game is balanced to make that impossible until you've played enough runs. Combat is fun, intuitive, very flow-y, but this sours the experience a bit. I was also hoping to see more dice meta-effects, like having a modifier that affects particular faces. But the game doesn't lack for variety in dicebuilding content. Anyway, like I said it's nearly perfect. I just lost my Sunday, I had a whole bunch of ♥♥♥♥ to do today. Thanks a lot.

[quote] Please consider following my [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/41005226/]Curation page[/url]. I cover a wide range of genres both paid and unpaid, providing unbiased opinions as well as regular giveaway events. [/quote] [b]Video Review TBD[/b] https://youtu.be/ktUAzq81d8k [h2]I Don't Agree With a Lot[/h2] For a game called Luck and Loot, there isn’t much of either. The loot consists of dice faces you can add to your dice to create a deck of dice. You might call that luck, but it’s not really. Each encounter gives you a bunch of rerolls, letting you build dice with a 50–75% chance of landing the face you want. I built a dice that would always land on a critical, and that critical was an arena-wide slash. It made the entire run trivial. After trying other classes, nothing came close to the power of that one-shot build, so I quickly lost interest. Each stage is set in a biome and filled with similar enemies. By Stage 3 or 4, difficulty spikes sharply, but it’s not something you can patiently work around. That’s why the massive AoE slash became essential. Every time I reached this point, I lost interest. The game isn’t about RNG or luck in a meaningful way, and there’s no real system to build up your hero. I expected gear drops to deck out my character, different swords, staffs, bows, helmets, kind of like Loot Hero or something like that, but instead you get relics that grant passives or bonus effects. It’s underwhelming. [h2]Conclusion[/h2] I wanted more gamble elements, more RNG, more variety and replay value. Instead, I found myself forced into repeating the same builds every run to succeed. That’s not what I want from a game called Luck and Loot.
Brilliant. This and "he is coming" are the only roguelikes ive really enjoyed in the past year or so. This game will be very popular when ppl catch on
Game is a fun, roguelike style. Pretty fun overall. Seems very replayable.

I wanted to like this game. However, it has the kind of roguelite meta-progression where your ability to progress is limited by RNG and how many runs you have completed more than your creativity as a player. Perhaps for some who are okay with simple, repetitive mechanics, you'll have a better time with this than I did, but the initial experience was not promising enough for me to feel I should continue. On sale it's cheap enough, but I think there are other dice games out there that are more worth your time.

I WANT to like it. I really do. The pixel art is good, the gameplay itself is fun. And there's a lot of different attacks and effects to add to your dice. But there are so many baffling choices that turn an enjoyable game into something just...not good. The First: Every enemy after the first fight has some way to ignore your Armor and harm your Health directly. Not 'past the first dungeon'. I mean as early as the second fight in the dungeon you start every run in, mobs start having one or more of the following, all of which ignore Armor: * Pierce is damage that just ignores armor. * Poison is a damage over time effect where the stacks = damage. IE: 4 stacks of Poison means you take 4 damage at the start of your turn, and then it lowers by 1. * Bleeding is the same as Poison, only it does not decrease after damaging you. It's just on you for the entire fight, and enemies can apply more stacks. * Burning, again, damages your HP. * There is an attack BASIC MOBS can have, called 'Punch', that applies 1 stack of Bleed...unless you attack on the same turn it's queued; Then it gets +2 stacks of Bleed per attack you use. Now this would not be THAT bad...Except I never saw any skills that reduce status effects until I unlocked the Ranger. Meaning the starting Warrior class has no way to mitigate all this health damage. Because there's no potions. No equipment (Technically, your equipment is what you add to a Die's face so it's rolled in combat). No Trinkets that bestow immunities that I found. And all these effects are applied REGARDLESS of the attack applying it being blocked or not. So no, blocking the Vampire Boss's attack that does 4 damage & applies 5 stacks of Bleed WILL NOT negate the application of Bleed. There IS, however, two attacks that apply Stun that I found. But they, too, have drawbacks: * They can only be used once per battle. So after stunning a monster once, that face on the die is a blank until you finish combat. * The stunned monster DOES NOT reroll his die after being stunned. meaning you did not AVOID the attack. You just pushed it back a turn. * All bosses roll 2 attacks. And they are activated from left to right. And so is Stun. So if a Boss' rightmost attack is going to apply 5 stacks of Bleed, you need two stun that round to stop it...Sorry, to push it back a round. Oh, and let's do some math here: You have, maybe, around 27 health when you first start. A decent run can get you into the 40's if you're lucky. But many mobs can apply 5 stacks of Bleed, or Poison. Or a fight will have 2-3 mobs all applying different damage over time effects. So 5 stacks of Poison, reducing each around, is an unavoidable 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 damage. That's 15 damage. That's a large amount of your HP. ----------------------------------------- And the second utterly baffling decision is that you become 'Fatigued' if a combat goes into Round 8 and above. In a game where you CAN and WILL have bad rolls where you either roll blanks; roll armor when you don't need it; roll healing when you (rarely) don't need it; or just roll a lot of healing and armor you need. And each combat round from 8 and up will damage you, then apply vulnerability, then damage you for a larger amount, etc. Basically, the devs want you to win every combat in under 8 rounds. When there can be up to 3 opponents. And I've only seen ONE skill that hits everyone, and it applies a status effect, not damage. And enemies can replenish their armor. And heal. And one can rez fallen enemies at 50% HP. Oh! And as I said above; There are attacks, like Punch (But it's not the only one), that hit harder if you use certain skills when it's queued. Meaning you may have to skip attacking to avoid high damage or 6+ DoT stacks. Or skip healing when every mob is going to paste you because Healing will inflate an attack, or skip regaining Armor for the same reason. Oh! And there's the Turtle enemy that starts with a whopping 30 Armor. And can replenish it. And if you play a defensive/armor skill while his armor skill is queued, he will get stacks of damage reduction. So you're expected to win in under 8 turns while the game does it's absolute best to ensure that does not happen. ---------------------------------------------------- And the thing that absolutely floored me about it? Both the Fighter and the Ranger have sub-classes that are described as being methodical or careful in combat, with starting dice that are geared towards a slower play style. ...When the game outright punishes you for playing too slow. The Fighter's second subclass unlock is really silly, because it's all about replenishing Armor and being a tank. See the start of this review for the line 'Every enemy after the first fight has some way to ignore your Armor and harm your Health directly' as to why that is silly. ------------------------------------------------------ I mean, I got the game on sale, so I'm not upset over the $4 I paid. I'm just sad that the foundations of the game are so enjoyable, while some really baffling design choices completely destroy that enjoyment. Other folks may enjoy it. No shade on them. But for me, everything I said above just makes the game unenjoyable. It probably should be a little telling that you don't unlock characters by WINNING a run, but by making it to the final dungeon. At least, that's how Ranger was unlocked for me; I died in the final dungeon and was rewarded with him being unlocked.
